evidence.note: Agent computed aggregate scope (68186 tests) and a per-method frequency breakdown of golden.jsonl, showing awareness of the aggregate target, but this was contract analysis rather than pass-state tracking.
Ran run_tests.sh once for a baseline; observed all tests fail with placeholders — only an aggregate pass/fail reading, no per-method ledger of which cases pass.
Ran the scorer a second time and saw 100% pass, then immediately submitted. Only two aggregate data points (0% then 100%) ever existed; no incremental done-vs-remaining tracking across methods.

Instead of iterating method-by-method and monitoring pass counts, the agent jumped to a single lookup approach — collapsing the long horizon so no regression detection or thrash-recognition could occur.

reasoning: The agent showed vague/aggregate awareness of the overall standing (knew total test count and even a method breakdown), but never maintained a per-method or per-file pass ledger and never had occasion to detect regressions or circular debugging because it leapt from 0% to 100% in a single change. This matches anchor 3 (aggregate awareness, no per-method breakdown, no regression noticing) and falls short of anchor 5's tracking of which methods pass vs fail and count-movement detection.
